1. "No longer would anyone have power over me now."
2. "The sacred relationship between the dreamer's body and the cathedral finds its immediate complement in the profane preoccupations of his waking life."
3. "Presence of the honored gods, those who gladly kept their oaths enjoy a life without tears, while the others undergo a toil that is unbearable to look at. Those who have persevered three times, on either side, to keep their souls free from all wrongdoing,"
4. "He who withholds not his heart's affection, but looks with a friendly eye on the welfare of his neighbor, and does not let his mind dwell on false thoughts, nor allow his tongue to utter unkind words, but loves his neighbor as himself: he who acts in this manner, and who is not afraid to confess his sins, or to bear his trials, for he knows that they are sent for his good, by Him who is his Father and his Friend; when such a one dies, he will enter the joys of the Lord, and will never more be separated from the presence of God."
5. "St. Peter showed them the way that leads to the gates of Paradise, which were made of pearl, and the streets thereof were paved with gold; and there they should behold the blessed souls of those who had done good works upon the earth. 'In groves we live,' said he, 'and lie on mossy beds, by crystal streams, that murmur through the meads; but pass yon easy hill, and thence descend, the path conducts you to your journey's end.'"

Please note that these are not continuous passages from the same text, and some of them have been paraphrased for clarity.
